title: Constructiones Participiales Provectae
subtitle: Vidi eum currentem — participium supplementarium, participia catenata, usus substantivus.
objectives: Uti participio supplementari post verba perceptionis (video, audio + accusativum + participium)
Distinguere participium supplementarium ab AcI (constructio similis, functio distincta)
Uti participiis substantive, sine nomine explicito
Legere catenas participiales multiplices in prosa densa

content.intro: 'Vidi milites hostibus victis, urbe capta, praeda divisa, domum revertentes,' legit Marcus ex Tacito. 'Vidi... revertentes' — participium supplementarium; tres ablativi absoluti catenati intra. Consolidamus hodie usus participii provectiores.
content.explanation:
“Vīdī mīlitēs, hostibus victīs, urbe captā, praedā dīvīsā, domum revertentēs,” legit Mārcus ex Tacitō. “'Vīdī... revertentēs' — nōn 'audīvī eōs revertisse' (factum reportātum), sed vīdī ipsum āctum, dīrēctē.” Iūlia adiungit: “Et 'victī' sōlum, sine 'mīlitēs', significat 'the defeated ones' — participium ut nōmen ipsum.”

Notāvistīne quot ūsūs participiī in ūnā sententiā Tacitī? Praeter ablātīvum absolūtum et participium concordāns simplex, Latīna habet aliōs ūsūs frequentēs in prōsā prōvectiōre — hodiē eōs cōnsolidāmus.

rules.heading: a) Participium Supplementarium (post Verba Perceptionis)
rules.body: Post videō, audiō, sentiō, obiectum accūsātīvum + participium (concordāns cum illō obiectō) dēscrībit āctiōnem PERCEPTAM DIRECTĒ: Vīdī puerum currentem. ('I saw the boy RUNNING' — vīdī ipsum āctum currendī, nōn tantum factum abstractum.) Compara cum AcI: Audīvī puerum cecidisse. ('I heard THAT the boy had fallen' — factum reportātum, nōn necessāriō vīsum/audītum dīrēctē.)

rules.heading: b) Participia Catenata
rules.body: Prōsa dēnsa (Tacitus praesertim) catenat multa participia sequentia: Mīlitēs, hostibus victīs, urbe captā, praedā dīvīsā, domum revertērunt. ('The soldiers, the enemy having been defeated, the city having been captured, the plunder having been divided, returned home' — trēs ablātīvī absolūtī sequentēs.)

rules.heading: c) Usus Substantivus
rules.body: Participium potest fungī ut nōmen ipsum, sine nōmine explicitō, praesertim in plūrālī: sapientēs ('the wise [men/people]' — ā sapiēns), dicta ('sayings, things said' — ā dictus, neutrum plūrāle), victī ('the defeated [ones]').

rules.heading: d) Distinctio Finalis: Quattuor Usus Simul
rules.body:
ConstructioExemplum
Concordans simplexMīlitēs victī fūgērunt.
Ablativus absolutusHostibus victīs, mīlitēs fūgērunt.
SupplementariumVīdī mīlitēs fugientēs.
SubstantivumVictī fūgērunt (nōn 'mīlitēs victī').

examples: Vidimus naves appropinquantes. — We saw the ships approaching.
Audivi te cantantem. — I heard you singing.
Fortes fortuna adiuvat. — Fortune favors the brave. (usus substantivus, proverbium)
Milites, hostibus victis, urbe capta, laeti domum redierunt. — The soldiers, the enemy defeated, the city captured, returned home joyfully.
Nemo sapientium hoc credidisset. — None of the wise men would have believed this.

commonMistakes.wrong: Participium supplementarium (video + acc. + part.) confunditur cum AcI, ambo tractati identice.
commonMistakes.right: Participium supplementarium indicat perceptionem DIRECTAM actus ('saw him running'); AcI indicat factum REPORTATUM ('heard that he had fallen').
commonMistakes.why: Distinctio semantica subtilis sed reālis: experientia sensualis directa vs. informatio reportata.

commonMistakes.wrong: Participium substantivum ('sapientes') tractatur ut requirens semper nomen explicitum concomitans.
commonMistakes.right: Participium potest stare solum, functionans ipse ut nomen ('the wise', 'the defeated'), sine nomine explicito necessario.
commonMistakes.why: Haec est extensio naturalis functionis adiectivalis participii — sicut quodvis adiectivum potest fungi substantive in Latina.

items.prompt: Differentia inter participium supplementarium et AcI est:
Nemo ___ hoc credidisset. (of the wise — sapientium)

summary: Participium supplementarium (video/audio + acc. + part.): perceptio directa actus.
Participia catenata: multiplices ablativi absoluti sequentes in prosa densa.
Usus substantivus: participium fungit ut nomen ipsum (sapientes, victi, dicta).
Quattuor usus participii nunc omnes noti: concordans, ablativus absolutus, supplementarium, substantivum.
